subject: Accounting
title: The Human Cost of Enron
description: One-minute skill: The Human Cost of Enron.

hook.text: 20,000 employees lost their jobs. Many lost their entire retirement savings in one week.

buildup.text: Enron encouraged workers to invest their 401(k) retirement funds in Enron stock.

discovery.text: When the stock crashed from $90 to $0.26, employee retirement accounts were wiped out.

twist.text: Executives sold their shares before the collapse. Employees were locked out from selling.

climax.text: CEO Ken Lay died before sentencing. CFO Fastow served six years. Others got longer.

punchline.text: Executives cashed out. Employees paid the price.

quiz.question: What happened to Enron employees' retirement savings?
options: They were wiped out when the stock crashed
They were transferred to other companies

details.summary: Beyond the financial numbers, Enron's collapse devastated real people—20,000 employees lost their jobs, retirement savings were wiped out, and communities that depended on the company suffered. This topic puts a human face on corporate fraud's consequences.
details.whyItMatters: Accounting fraud isn't an abstract financial crime. Real people lose their livelihoods, life savings, and sometimes their lives. The human cost is what makes preventing fraud a moral imperative.
takeaways: Employees who invested retirement savings in Enron stock lost everything when the stock went to zero
Workers were locked out of selling their 401(k) shares during the stock's steepest decline
The suicide of Enron executive Cliff Baxter highlighted the personal toll on all involved

faq.question: How did Enron's collapse affect its employees?
faq.answer: About 20,000 employees lost their jobs. Many had invested heavily in Enron stock through their 401(k) plans and lost their entire retirement savings. During the stock's steepest decline, employees were locked out of selling shares during an administrative transfer period.

faq.question: What happened to the people involved in the Enron scandal?
faq.answer: CEO Jeff Skilling was sentenced to 24 years (later reduced to 14). CFO Andrew Fastow got 6 years. Founder Ken Lay was convicted but died before sentencing. Executive Cliff Baxter committed suicide. Thousands of innocent employees suffered job losses and financial ruin.
